input.baseline: 60 kg for 5 reps, 3 sets. I lift 3 days a week, with a rack and a spotter.

baselineMeasurements.sourceQuote: 60 kg for 5 reps, 3 sets. I lift 3 days a week

options.rationale: A patient climb of about 0.7 kg a week from 60 kg to 80 kg for 5 reps, keeping your 3 days and adding load in small steps with deload weeks.
assumptions: You keep lifting 3 days a week with a rack and spotter
Recovery, sleep and food stay steady
Load rises about 2.5 kg every 3 to 4 weeks
Deload weeks may be needed if reps slip

cases.title: First half marathon, one day a week (mine)

input.baseline: I run 3 km once a week at an easy pace.

asked.question: Do you have a finish time in mind?

coachNote.message: A first half marathon needs at least 3 runs a week to build safely, so both plans use 3–4 days. You can start with your 1 day and add runs gradually.

baselineMeasurements.sourceQuote: I run 3 km once a week at an easy pace.
I run 3 km once a week at an easy pace.

options.rationale: A patient build from one 3 km run a week to a first half marathon, with gradual increases, a long run that grows slowly and a short taper.
assumptions: You stay healthy and can train 3 days a week.
Weekly distance grows about 10% on average, with easier weeks.
No finish time target, so success is completing 21.1 km.
Easy pace is by feel until you log a few runs.

phases.progressCheck: Long run reaches 14 km and weekly total about 25 km without lingering soreness.

phases.progressCheck: Complete a long run of 18 to 19 km at an easy effort.

phases.title: Taper and race
phases.progressCheck: Volume drops, you feel fresh, and you start the half marathon rested.

options.rationale: Three or four running days a week with gradual weekly growth from 3 km, aiming to complete a first half marathon with no time target.

Easy pace is felt by effort, since no pace was given

window.summary: Your 10 October run felt hard, so I've eased the next two weeks to shorter, gentler easy runs on three days a week, without adding back anything you missed. The goal stays the same, and I've given the first phase one extra week so the 5 km base can feel comfortable.
